events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.tick.EntityTickEvent.Post - the module's only handler (GliderWaterRepairModule.java:80-100, @SubscribeEvent on the instance registered to NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize, line 68). The event fires on both sides for every ticking entity; the body bails unless the entity is an ItemEntity, its tickCount is a multiple of 20, isModuleEnabled(), the level is a ServerLevel and the item is in water.
notes:
SCOPE LIMIT (the single most important thing for a doc writer): only a **dropped item entity** lying in water is freed. onItemEntityTick filters `event.getEntity() instanceof ItemEntity` (GliderWaterRepairModule.java:82) - a broken paraglider in the inventory, in the chest armor slot or in a Curios back slot is never touched. The player has to actually throw it in the water. The predecessor module searched Curios slots; that lookup was deliberately dropped together with the lightning protection ("Die Curios-Suche entfaellt mit dem Blitzschutz, weil nur noch fallengelassene Items zaehlen", commit e7469c4). README.md:151 never says it ("dunking it works"); docs/modules/glider_water_repair.md says "lying in water as a dropped item" exactly once, at line 49.

GUARD ORDER / THROTTLE: the handler returns unless, in this order (lines 82-88), the entity is an ItemEntity, `itemEntity.tickCount % WATER_CHECK_INTERVAL == 0` (interval = 20), isModuleEnabled(), `itemEntity.level() instanceof ServerLevel`, and `itemEntity.isInWater()`. So one check per second per dropped item - up to ~1 s delay after it hits the water, which is intentional ("das Ding muss ohnehin erst sinken", e7469c4) - and nothing at all runs on a client. isInWater() is water, not rain (vanilla semantics, not provable from this repo).

WHAT IS AND IS NOT RESTORED: the entire effect is `stack.set(requireBrokenComponent(), false)` (line 94). Durability is not touched, so the anvil plus the tier-matched Reinforced Paper stays the only way to get the damage bar back. The lightning mechanic itself (Gliders' GliderUtil.lightningLogic / GliderItem.setBroken) is left completely alone - this module contains no lightning code whatsoever. Verified OUTSIDE the repo in gliders-1.21.1-neoforge-1.1.8.jar: GliderItem.isGlidingEnabled == (GLIDE component present and true) && !isBroken, and GliderItem.isTooBroken (damage >= maxDamage - 1) is defined but called nowhere in that jar - so clearing the flag alone really does restore gliding, however low the durability is. The vc_gliders:struck flag is not cleared either, but the mod resets it itself (GliderUtil.onTickPlayerGlide calls setStruck(stack, false) once flying is blocked), so a water-repaired glider can be struck again.

FEEDBACK: SoundEvents.FIRE_EXTINGUISH (SoundSource.NEUTRAL, volume 0.7F, pitch 1.2F) plus 8 ParticleTypes.CLOUD particles at y+0.2 with spread 0.2/0.1/0.2 and speed 0.0, both emitted server-side (level.playSound(null, ...), level.sendParticles), so clients without the module still see and hear the repair; the cleared flag itself reaches them through the ordinary ItemEntity stack sync. One debug log line ("Water freed {} from its broken state").

ITEM DETECTION IS A PREFIX MATCH: isGlider (lines 102-108) accepts any item whose registry key has namespace `vc_gliders` AND whose path startsWith("paraglider"). Which ids that hits is NOT provable from this repository - no compile dependency on Gliders, no jar in libs/, no mention of vc_gliders outside this module's own source and doc. Verified OUTSIDE the repo against ~/.minecraft-instances/sebsmodpack4/mods/gliders-1.21.1-neoforge-1.1.8.jar: assets/vc_gliders/lang/en_us.json contains exactly five item.vc_gliders.paraglider_* keys (paraglider_wood, _iron, _gold, _diamond, _netherite), so the prefix currently matches all five tiers and nothing else (the mod's remaining items are copper_upgrade, nether_upgrade and reinforced_paper*). The paraglider_*_copper_upgrade / _nether_upgrade / _combined_upgrades files under models/item are item-property overrides on `upgrade_level`, not separate items - the same override list switches to damaged_glider at upgrade_level 0.4, which is the charred sprite the README talks about. If Gliders ever renames its items, detection stops silently with no log line.

COMPONENT LOOKUP IS ONE-SHOT: requireBrokenComponent() (lines 119-131) resolves vc_gliders:broken from BuiltInRegistries.DATA_COMPONENT_TYPE lazily and caches the result behind brokenComponentResolved. If it is absent on that first lookup, a warning is logged **once** and the field stays null for the rest of the session - there is no retry, isBroken() then returns false for everything and the module simply goes quiet. The cast to DataComponentType<Boolean> is unchecked (@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")). Verified OUTSIDE the repo: vc_gliders' ItemComponentRegistry registers copper_upgrade, nether_upgrade, glide, broken and struck with Codec.BOOL, and GliderItem.isBroken reads the value as a Boolean - so the cast is correct against 1.1.8.

RUNTIME TOGGLE IS ONE-WAY: isModuleEnabled() is re-checked inside the handler and resolves the live config value plus any /vpa module enable|disable override (AbstractModule.java:202-214 -> ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled, ModuleManager.java:205-208), so switching the module OFF takes effect immediately. Switching it ON at runtime does nothing: ModuleManager.initializeModules only calls initialize() for modules that were enabled when the config was first read (ModuleManager.java:104-107), and only onInitialize() registers the handler on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS (line 68). A module that started disabled - or started without Gliders present - needs a restart.

NO DEPENDENCY IS DECLARED ANYWHERE: src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml declares optional dependencies for create, toughasnails, sable and bluemap, but has no vc_gliders entry, and the generated standalone toml (build.gradle renderModuleToml, lines 507-530) emits only vpa_core / neoforge / minecraft plus the incompatible-with-bundle entry. Gliders is found purely through ModList.get().isLoaded at runtime; without it AbstractModule.initialize logs "Module 'Glider Water Repair' is disabled and will not be initialized" and nothing else happens. README.md:237 lists the module in the integration table with the correct note ("Module skips initialization entirely").

HISTORY / MIGRATION: the module replaces glider_lightning_guard in a single commit, e7469c4 (2026-09-18), which deleted the old module, its Curios compat classes (CuriosGate, GliderCuriosAccess), its config and docs/glider_lightning_guard.md. The lightning protection was removed without replacement by design ("die Gefahr im Gewitter ist der Sinn der Mechanik"). IMPORTANT correction to the obvious assumption: the predecessor NEVER shipped in a tagged release - it was added in 1ea3133 and removed in e7469c4, and the tags jump v1.0.0-beta.81 -> v1.0.0-beta.86 both locally and on origin, so the CHANGELOG entries for beta.82 through beta.85 have no tag behind them. Only someone who ran a build made from that commit window carries the old state: for them the config section was renamed glider_lightning_guard -> glider_water_repair and the old durability_cost key is gone, so leftover entries in an existing toml are dead. First tag containing this module: v1.0.0-beta.86 (git tag --contains e7469c4).

DOC DRIFT (working copy, uncommitted): the in-flight docs reorg has moved the doc to docs/modules/glider_water_repair.md (staged rename; HEAD still carries docs/glider_water_repair.md), but README.md:151 and README.md:305 still link docs/glider_water_repair.md, which no longer exists on disk - both links are stale. Also, the Configuration table in docs/modules/glider_water_repair.md (lines 80-82) lists only `enabled` and omits `debug_logging`, which AbstractModuleConfig.buildConfig adds to every module (AbstractModuleConfig.java:62-66).

NO ASSETS AT ALL: no lang keys (no "glider" in any file under assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/), no items, blocks or entities, no commands, no keybinds, no mixins (no mixin/glider_water_repair/ package, no entry in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json, and the build.gradle standaloneModules row at line 435 is bare - no mixins, no clientMixins, no dataGlobs), no recipes, no loot-table hooks, no data files. Three source files in total: modules/glider_water_repair/GliderWaterRepairModule.java (132 lines), modules/glider_water_repair/config/GliderWaterRepairConfig.java (18 lines - an empty subclass that does not override buildModuleSpecificConfig and does not override isEnabledByDefault) and standalone/glider_water_repair/GliderWaterRepairStandalone.java (20 lines, @Mod("vpa_glider_water_repair") delegating to StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot). No TODO/FIXME comments anywhere in it.
oneLiner: A paraglider from the Gliders mod that a lightning strike left broken can be thrown into water - as a dropped item, never one sitting in a slot: it hisses, steams and glides again, though it stays as battered as the strike left it.

requiredMods.evidence: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/glider_water_repair/GliderWaterRepairModule.java:61-64 - shouldInitialize() { return ModList.get().isLoaded("vc_gliders"); }, which is the hard gate: AbstractModule.initialize returns before onInitialize when it is false (core/AbstractModule.java:90-105), so no event handler is ever registered. Nothing declares the dependency statically - no vc_gliders entry in src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml and none in the generated standalone toml (build.gradle:507-530). The mod is "Gliders" on Modrinth; verified outside the repo as gliders-1.21.1-neoforge-1.1.8.jar.

shortDescription: A broken Gliders paraglider thrown into water becomes usable again
